_comment: Serving budgets. Derived from four repeated baseline runs on 22-09-2026 (A100 40GB,
Qwen3-14B-AWQ + Qwen3-4B-AWQ behind vLLM), not from targets — model/bench/baselines/
holds two of those runs.
What is NOT gated here matters as much as what is. The same four runs measured
time-to-first-token at concurrency 8 anywhere between 62ms and 4025ms for one profile,
because this GPU also serves the deployed stack. A bound wide enough to survive that
would catch nothing; a bound tight enough to be useful would fail on other people's
traffic. So latency-under-load is measured, reported, and deliberately left unjudged.
Three things ARE stable enough to gate, and each catches a regression that is
otherwise silent:
prompt_tokens_max  — deterministic. Fails when a system prompt grows. This is the
cheapest regression to introduce (edit a .txt) and the one
nothing else in the repo notices.
decode_tps_min     — varied under 1% run to run at concurrency 1. Fails when a model,
a quantisation or a kernel got slower. Only set where the forced
output is long enough to measure: guardrail generates 64 tokens
and its decode rate came back bimodal (84 or 220 tok/s across
four runs), so it has no floor rather than a floor that lies.
prefix_cache_hit_rate_min — fails when something per-request gets placed ahead of the
stable prefix, which costs a full prefill and shows up nowhere
else. Held loose where the baseline itself is loose.
Judged at concurrency 1 only — the quiet, reproducible scenario. decode_tps is judged
only on a --force-output report, because a judge that naturally emits twelve tokens has
no decode rate worth comparing.

guardrail._why_no_decode_floor: 64 forced tokens measured 84 or 220 tok/s across four runs — the window is too short to be a measurement.

planner._why: The largest fixed prefix in the product (~1.9k tokens) on every request. Its cache hit rate sat at 99-100% across every run; anything lower means the prefix stopped being shared.

judge._why: Hit rate baselines at 78-84%, not higher, because the judge's user turn is most of its prompt. Held at the measured floor rather than an aspiration.

text_to_sql._why: The schema block is capped at 6000 chars by handlers/data.py. If prompt_tokens goes over this bound, that cap stopped holding.

responder._why_hit_rate_is_zero: Measured at 6%. responder_system.txt is 26 bytes, so there is no shared prefix to cache and the whole 1.8k-token context is prefilled every request — this is the finding the baseline produced, recorded as a bound of zero so it is impossible to mistake for a healthy number. Raise it the day the prompt is restructured; do not lower anything else to match it.

_why: Errors are absolute: a benchmark that measured six of eight requests measured a
different workload. Preemption means vLLM ran out of KV room and evicted running
requests — every latency in that scenario belongs to a saturated server, so the
report should be rejected rather than read.
